Quantization changes how the same numeric weights are stored; a genuinely smaller Dense student changes the architecture first, with distillation only changing its learning target. The new definitions make joint the jointly trained text/image/audio model and DPO a subsequent preference comparison branch, so the chosen DPO teacher is distinct from the recommended joint source. In the one-layer example, 32 weights and four biases need 144 FP32 bytes, while 4-bit packed weights plus row scales and biases need 48 bytes; finer 8-bit storage uses 64 bytes. Fewer stored bytes do not prove faster CPU arithmetic or smaller loaded-model RAM. The cited PTQ table retains 78/90 accuracy even when a generated answer changes, and the smaller students score CE 62/90 versus KD 61/90. I can now interpret the task subsets: full tool loops, independently supplied tool results, exact digit copying and square/circle recognition test different abilities inside the same 90 questions. The new glossary covers the component and file terminology I previously could not explain. All three first-round issues are concretely closed; I found no remaining readability obstacle in this assigned section.

program_explanation.details: I reread the complete current Python fence and its prose. Seed 42 fixes initialization; Linear(8,4) gives four outputs from eight features with 32 weights and four biases; QuantizedLinear is made from that original layer. ones(1,8) supplies one all-ones row and both outputs have shape (1,4). no_grad means no gradient accumulation and no training. Corresponding outputs are subtracted, made absolute, maximized across four entries, and extracted with item. Parameter element counts times element sizes give 144 original bytes; storage_bytes counts the quantized tensor payload, not file/Python/runtime overhead. The exact current fence was byte-compared to the genuinely executed first-round script and matches. own_explanation.problem: A smaller computer may need a smaller download/weight file, a smaller model architecture, or both. Quantization stores fewer bits for some weights and can alter answers. Distillation requires selecting a genuinely smaller student first, then checking whether a fixed teacher helps that student preserve abilities.
own_explanation.branches_and_components: joint is the result of text/image/audio joint training. DPO continues from joint using better/worse answer pairs, and is a comparison branch here. The recommended joint PTQ delivery and the DPO-derived student experiments therefore concern different source weights. A material connector maps image/audio features into language-core vectors; an embedding maps an input ID to a vector; normalization changes feature center/scale; router selects experts. The deployment format quantizes non-router Linear weights but retains embedding, normalization, bias and router as FP32. Per-output-channel means one scale for each output-weight row.
own_explanation.code_input_and_output: The original code creates one seeded Linear with 8 input features and 4 outputs, then quantizes that layer. A single row of eight ones produces four outputs. The maximum of their absolute differences measures only that one input. Original tensor bytes are (32+4)*4=144. 4-bit weight payload is 32*4/8=16 bytes, plus four FP32 scales=16 and four FP32 biases=16, making 48. First-round actual difference was 0.046346306800842285. Changing only bits to 8 gives 32+16+16=64 bytes and first-round actual difference 0.0037038326263427734; this round compared exact code bytes and reused those saved outputs.
own_explanation.formula: The KD objective is 0.5 CE + 0.5 T^2 KL(p_T||q_T), with T=2. CE measures error on the true answer. p_T is the fixed teacher distribution and q_T the student distribution at the same temperature; each comes from softmax(scores/T), which shows secondary candidates more clearly at larger T. KL(p||q)=sum_i p_i(log p_i-log q_i) uses teacher probabilities to weight corresponding candidates. The helper already includes T^2=4, so the caller applies only the 0.5 mixture coefficient and does not multiply by four again. The teacher stays fixed and only the student learns.
own_explanation.relevant_numbers: The cited joint FP32/4-bit/8-bit files are 1,345,023/275,381/429,365 bytes, while their tensor payloads are 1,312,512/248,864/402,720. Each scores 78/90, but 4-bit changes one generated ID sequence and 8-bit has no observed sequence change on those 90 questions. The DPO comparison changes two 4-bit sequences at the same score. The two-layer width-48 Dense student has 79,920 parameters, hence 319,680 FP32 tensor bytes. CE and KD share a random starting point, seed/batch rules, 350 updates and 145,163 effective answer positions. Each scores 59/84 on validation; final whole-question scores are 62/90 and 61/90. The KD 4-bit tensor payload is 91,680 bytes and cited file 106,229; it stays at 61/90 although six actions/final ID sequences change on already wrong questions. These are historical results in the prose, not models I trained or reloaded.
own_explanation.how_to_interpret_task_counts: Paired counts list CE then KD. Full tool loops are 1/12 and 0/12: a correct request, real tool execution and a correct model read-back answer are required. Independent refill is 1/6 for each: question and tool result are supplied directly, skipping the first request. Exact digit copying is 0/3 for each, and square/circle shape identification 0/9 for each. These are subsets of the same 90-question final check and are not extra questions to add to the total. The linked action/EOS explanation lets me distinguish a valid prefix, a correct complete request and successful final answer.
own_explanation.how_to_check_the_exercise: Keep the same seed, weights and input; change only bits to 8; predict packed-weight bytes separately from scale/bias overhead; compare the two print lines. For a complete saved delivery, reload it and check common held-out tasks and individual responses as well as file/tensor sizes; loaded RAM, speed and peak memory need separate measurement.
